common_name: SunPatiens Compact Magenta Impatiens (Sun-Tolerant Season-Long Bedding Impatiens)

planting.note: Set out transplants after the last frost into full sun to partial shade in fertile, well-drained soil; Magenta is one of the vivid solid colors bred into the compact tier of the SunPatiens line, holding a tight, mounded habit suited to beds and containers.

directions: Plant in full sun to partial shade in fertile, well-drained soil, feeding on a regular schedule to sustain the season-long bloom this vegetatively propagated series is known for. SunPatiens Compact Magenta forms a dense, self-branching mound smothered in vivid magenta-pink flowers from spring planting through the first hard frost, holding its shape and color better through summer heat than older New Guinea impatiens types. Because it carries strong resistance to impatiens downy mildew, it performs reliably in beds where common Impatiens walleriana has failed in recent years. Keep soil evenly moist, especially in containers, since the compact habit has a smaller root volume to draw on during hot, dry stretches.

common_name: SunPatiens Compact Blush Pink Impatiens (Sun-Tolerant Season-Long Bedding Impatiens)
scientific_name: Impatiens x hybrida 'SunPatiens Compact Blush Pink'

planting.note: Set out transplants after the last frost into full sun to partial shade in fertile, well-drained soil; Blush Pink is a soft pastel shade within the compact tier of the SunPatiens line, holding a tight, mounded habit suited to beds and containers.

directions: Plant in full sun to partial shade in fertile, well-drained soil, feeding regularly through the growing season to keep the dense mound flowering nonstop. SunPatiens Compact Blush Pink produces a gentle wash of pale pink blooms over glossy dark green foliage, a softer complement to the more saturated colors in the SunPatiens line, while sharing the same heat tolerance and resistance to downy mildew that let it thrive where older impatiens types decline in summer. The compact habit stays tidy without pinching, making it useful for mass bedding, edging, and mixed containers. Water deeply and consistently, particularly in the heat of midsummer, to prevent wilting between waterings.

common_name: SunPatiens Compact Deep Rose Impatiens (Sun-Tolerant Season-Long Bedding Impatiens)
scientific_name: Impatiens x hybrida 'SunPatiens Compact Deep Rose'

planting.note: Set out transplants after the last frost into full sun to partial shade in fertile, well-drained soil; Deep Rose is a richly saturated color within the compact tier of the SunPatiens line, holding a tight, mounded habit suited to beds and containers.

directions: Plant in full sun to partial shade in fertile, well-drained soil, and feed on a consistent schedule to sustain vigorous, nonstop bloom through the heat of summer. SunPatiens Compact Deep Rose covers its tidy, well-branched mound in rich rose-pink flowers from spring planting until frost, offering a deeper, more saturated color option within the compact tier of the series. Like its SunPatiens relatives, it tolerates far more direct sun and heat than traditional shade impatiens and carries strong resistance to impatiens downy mildew. Keep the root zone evenly moist, especially in containers or raised beds that dry out quickly in summer heat.

common_name: SunPatiens Vigorous Magenta New Guinea Impatiens (Large Vase-Habit Downy-Mildew-Resistant Impatiens)

planting.note: Plant transplants after all frost danger has passed in moist, well-drained soil in partial shade to full sun; SunPatiens Vigorous Magenta is the large-form, vase-habit tier of the SunPatiens line, reaching 30-36 inches, with strong resistance to downy mildew.

directions: Plant in moist, humus-rich, well-drained soil in partial shade to full sun, watering regularly to keep the root zone consistently moist. SunPatiens Vigorous Magenta is the large-form, vase-shaped tier of the SunPatiens breeding line, reaching 30 to 36 inches tall and covered in bright magenta-pink flowers from spring through frost, a far bigger scale than the compact or spreading SunPatiens forms. It shares the line's strong resistance to downy mildew and tolerates considerably more sun than traditional shade impatiens while still flowering well in partial shade. Its size and vigor make it a good choice as a seasonal flowering hedge, back-of-border planting, or large container centerpiece, and it needs no deadheading to stay in continuous bloom.

common_name: SunPatiens Vigorous Red New Guinea Impatiens (Large Vase-Habit Downy-Mildew-Resistant Impatiens)

planting.note: Plant transplants after all frost danger has passed in moist, well-drained soil in partial shade to full sun; SunPatiens Vigorous Red is the large-form, vase-habit tier of the SunPatiens line, reaching 30-36 inches, with strong resistance to downy mildew.

directions: Plant in moist, humus-rich, well-drained soil in partial shade to full sun, keeping the soil consistently moist through the growing season. SunPatiens Vigorous Red is the largest-growing tier of the SunPatiens line, forming an upright, vase-shaped plant 30 to 36 inches tall smothered in bright true-red flowers from spring planting through the first hard frost. Like the rest of the series it resists the downy mildew that devastated older impatiens plantings and tolerates far more direct sun than traditional shade impatiens while still thriving in partial shade. Its substantial size suits it to large containers, mixed borders, and mass plantings where a bold, season-long red is wanted.

common_name: SunPatiens Vigorous White Improved New Guinea Impatiens (Large Vase-Habit Downy-Mildew-Resistant Impatiens)
scientific_name: Impatiens x hybrida 'SunPatiens Vigorous White Improved'

planting.note: Plant transplants after all frost danger has passed in moist, well-drained soil in partial shade to full sun; SunPatiens Vigorous White Improved is the large-form, vase-habit tier of the SunPatiens line, reaching 30-36 inches, with strong resistance to downy mildew.

directions: Plant in moist, humus-rich, well-drained soil in partial shade to full sun, and water on a consistent schedule since large plants draw more moisture through the summer. SunPatiens Vigorous White Improved is a refined, more floriferous version of the original Vigorous White selection, forming a substantial vase-shaped plant 30 to 36 inches tall covered in clean white flowers against dark green foliage from spring through frost. It carries the same strong resistance to downy mildew as the rest of the SunPatiens line and tolerates far more sun than traditional impatiens while still performing well in partial shade. Its bright, luminous flowers make it especially effective for lighting up shaded corners and evening gardens, and no deadheading is needed to keep it blooming.

common_name: Divine Scarlet Red New Guinea Impatiens (Seed-Grown Heat-Tolerant Impatiens)

planting.note: Start seed indoors 10-12 weeks before the last frost date, since Divine is a true seed-propagated New Guinea impatiens rather than a cutting-grown hybrid; transplant out after all danger of frost has passed into partial shade to partial sun.

directions: Sow seed indoors 10 to 12 weeks before the last frost date at a warm 70 to 80°F, since Divine is a seed-propagated New Guinea impatiens series bred as a more economical, easy-to-grow alternative to the cutting-propagated SunPatiens and Infinity lines. Divine Scarlet Red produces vivid, saturated scarlet-red flowers over a compact, well-branched mound from planting until frost, and like other New Guinea impatiens hybrids it tolerates considerably more sun than common Impatiens walleriana while still performing best with some afternoon shade in hot climates. It carries good resistance to impatiens downy mildew, making it a dependable substitute where traditional bedding impatiens have struggled. Keep the soil evenly moist and feed lightly through the season to sustain continuous bloom.

common_name: Divine Orange New Guinea Impatiens (Seed-Grown Bronze-Leaf Impatiens)

planting.note: Start seed indoors 10-12 weeks before the last frost date, since Divine is a true seed-propagated New Guinea impatiens rather than a cutting-grown hybrid; transplant out after all danger of frost has passed into partial shade to partial sun.

directions: Sow seed indoors 10 to 12 weeks before the last frost date at a warm 70 to 80°F, since Divine is a seed-propagated New Guinea impatiens series bred to offer growers an economical, easy-to-germinate alternative to vegetatively propagated New Guinea impatiens. Divine Orange bears bright orange flowers set against distinctive bronze-tinted foliage, a striking combination that sets it apart from the plain green-leaved colors in the series. It tolerates considerably more sun than common Impatiens walleriana, performing best with morning sun and afternoon shade in hot climates, and carries good resistance to impatiens downy mildew. Keep soil consistently moist and provide light regular feeding to sustain continuous bloom from spring through frost.

common_name: Kauai Burgundy Wishbone Flower (Compact Shade Torenia)

planting.note: Plant transplants after all frost danger has passed in moist, well-drained soil in partial to full shade; Kauai Burgundy is part of a compact, early-flowering wishbone flower series bred for uniform bloom timing across the color range.

directions: Plant in moist, humus-rich, well-drained soil in partial to full shade, keeping the soil consistently damp through summer heat. Kauai Burgundy carries deep wine-red flowers on a tidy, mounding plant, part of a compact wishbone flower series bred for early, uniform flowering across its color range so that mixed plantings bloom together. It thrives in shaded spots where many bedding annuals struggle, flowering continuously from late spring through frost with good heat and humidity tolerance and no deadheading required. Regular watering during dry spells keeps the display dense and full.

common_name: Kauai Magenta Wishbone Flower (Compact Shade Torenia)

planting.note: Plant transplants after all frost danger has passed in moist, well-drained soil in partial to full shade; Kauai Magenta is part of a compact, early-flowering wishbone flower series bred for uniform bloom timing across the color range.

directions: Plant in moist, humus-rich, well-drained soil in partial to full shade, watering regularly to keep the root zone consistently moist through summer. Kauai Magenta produces vivid magenta-pink flowers with a small yellow throat marking on a compact, mounding plant, part of an early-flowering wishbone flower series bred for uniform bloom timing across its color range. It performs reliably in shaded beds and containers where many flowering annuals falter, blooming continuously from late spring through frost without deadheading. Consistent moisture and light monthly feeding keep the display full and vivid through the hottest part of the season.

common_name: Kauai Lemon Drop Wishbone Flower (Compact Yellow Shade Torenia)

planting.note: Plant transplants after all frost danger has passed in moist, well-drained soil in partial to full shade; Kauai Lemon Drop is part of a compact, early-flowering wishbone flower series bred for uniform bloom timing across the color range.

directions: Plant in moist, humus-rich, well-drained soil in partial to full shade, keeping the soil consistently moist through the growing season. Kauai Lemon Drop bears soft lemon-yellow flowers, an unusual and useful color for brightening shaded beds and containers where the genus is more typically grown in blues, pinks, and purples. As part of the early-flowering Kauai series, it blooms uniformly with its series-mates and flowers continuously from late spring through frost without deadheading. Good drainage combined with steady moisture keeps plants compact and floriferous through summer heat and humidity.

common_name: Catalina Pink Torenia (Heat-Tolerant Trailing Wishbone Flower)

planting.note: Plant after all frost danger has passed; part of the Catalina series of heat-tolerant trailing torenia bred by PanAmerican Seed.

directions: Plant in shade to partial shade in moist, well-drained, fertile soil. Catalina Pink bears two-tone pink, snapdragon-like flowers with a soft yellow-marked throat, part of the Catalina series bred for improved heat tolerance and a semi-trailing habit suited to hanging baskets, window boxes, and shaded beds alike. It flowers continuously through the hottest part of summer without deadheading, giving reliable color in shaded spots where many other annuals falter. Consistent moisture and a mostly shaded position keep the trailing stems full and the display bright through Gulf South-style heat and humidity.

common_name: Catalina White Linen Torenia (Heat-Tolerant Trailing Wishbone Flower)

planting.note: Plant after all frost danger has passed; part of the Catalina series of heat-tolerant trailing torenia bred by PanAmerican Seed.

directions: Plant in shade to partial shade in moist, well-drained, fertile soil. Catalina White Linen bears pure white, snapdragon-like flowers with a faint yellow throat, offering a bright, luminous option within the heat-tolerant, semi-trailing Catalina series. It performs well in hanging baskets, window boxes, and shaded beds, flowering continuously through summer heat without deadheading. Consistent moisture keeps the trailing habit lush and prevents the leaf scorch that can occur if plants dry out in bright conditions.

common_name: Blue Bells Browallia (Classic Lavender-Blue Bush Violet)

planting.note: Plant transplants after all frost danger has passed in moist, well-drained soil in partial to full shade; Blue Bells is one of the classic older Browallia speciosa selections, valued for its abundant lavender-blue, star-shaped flowers.

directions: Plant in moist, humus-rich, well-drained soil in partial to full shade, keeping the soil evenly moist through the growing season. Blue Bells is a classic Browallia speciosa selection prized for its abundant lavender-blue, star-shaped flowers with a small white eye, held above soft, light green foliage on a compact, mounding plant. It thrives in the same shaded, humid conditions where impatiens and torenia perform well, blooming continuously from planting until frost without deadheading. Light monthly feeding and consistent watering keep the display dense, since Browallia's fine root system is less drought-tolerant than many other shade annuals.
